rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the foremost and greatest expression of gratitude to God.
rows.anchor: It is the foremost and the greatest manifestation of gratitude to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All prophets and divine religions have taught people to pray.
rows.anchor: All prophets of God and all divine religions unanimously have taught people to pray.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counsel means diligent prayer: he should pray himself, arrange for others to pray, and urge them to it.
rows.anchor: not only adhere to the prayer himself, but make arrangements for others also

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining maʿrūf is the second expression of gratitude and connects a person to fellow people, whereas prayer connects him to God.
rows.anchor: It connects a person to his brethren. The prayer, on the other hand, connects a person to his Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿrūf covers fulfillment of rights, including charity, aid to orphans and needy people, help for neighbours, and familiar acts of kindness.
rows.anchor: spending in the way of God, helping orphans, the destitute, neighbours and all other people in need

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forbidding wrong means abstaining from conduct opposed to maʿrūf, such as stinginess, usurping rights, injustice, broken promises, and conceit.
rows.anchor: include stinginess, usurpation of rights, injustice, breaking promises, conceit etc.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoining good and forbidding wrong bring hardship at every step, so they require patience and perseverance to make progress.
rows.anchor: if he does not exercise patience, he will not be able to take a single step ahead.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These tasks cannot be done half-heartedly; they demand full force, perseverance, and a willingness to stake one’s life on succeeding.
rows.anchor: these tasks cannot be carried out half-heartedly. Only those people can accomplish them who stand up with full force and perseverance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is why Sūrat al-ʿAṣr also mentions steadfastness and patience in upholding the truth.
rows.anchor: In Sūrah al-‘Aṣr, it is precisely for this reason that showing steadfastness and patience on the truth is mentioned.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression about turning one’s cheek means showing people indifference out of arrogance and haughtiness.
rows.anchor: means to show indifference to people because of arrogance and haughtiness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People” particularly refers to the masses, including poor and needy people whom the rich look down upon.
rows.anchor: the poor and needy who are looked down upon by the rich.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility manifests gratitude and arrogance is its opposite; mean people can become arrogant after receiving favours and look down on those beneath them, an attitude Luqmān forbids.
rows.anchor: humility is the manifestation of gratitude and the opposite of humility is arrogance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel warning in Banī Isrāʾīl says that a person cannot pierce the earth or reach the mountains’ height, exposing the futility of arrogant posturing.
rows.anchor: he cannot pierce the earth or climb as high as the mountains.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance is especially baseless in God’s kingdom, where everyone witnesses His power and exaltedness.
rows.anchor: What is the meaning of showing arrogance in the kingdom of God Whose signs of power and exaltedness everyone witnesses?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God dislikes the arrogant and haughty; Luqmān warns people of wealth and status not to mistake divine favours for personal entitlement, but to regard them as a gift and test.
rows.anchor: God does not like a person who is arrogant and haughty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s face, neck, and gait reveal arrogance, and Luqmān prohibits both forms of arrogant display.
rows.anchor: The arrogance and conceit of a person is evident from his face and neck and also from his gait.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding verse’s prohibitions, Luqmān positively directs his son to walk humbly and speak politely rather than rudely.
rows.anchor: In this verse, Luqmān has directed his son in a positive way to adopt humility

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occurrence of min indicates that people’s voices have different pitches and that they can raise or lower them as needed, rather than continually burdening others’ ears.
rows.anchor: God has not created mankind with the same pitch in their voices.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the donkey’s bray the ugliest voice warns people against coarse and impolite tones.
rows.anchor: are meant to stop people from being coarse and impolite in their tone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People made in the best form and blessed with eloquent speech disgrace themselves if they become like donkeys; doing so is utter misfortune.
rows.anchor: blessed them with quality of eloquent speech, why should they fall from this status and become donkeys. It is their utter misfortune if they do this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqmān’s counsel benefits everyone but has special force for leaders with political authority, since it prepares his son for leadership responsibilities.
rows.anchor: they carry special significance for those who are in the position of leadership and have political authority.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi describes Luqmān as a sage and political ruler, not a prophet, while seeing a general resemblance to the prophet David.
rows.anchor: Luqmān was not a prophet; however he does have a general resemblance with the prophet David (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section III begins by returning to Luqmān’s foremost counsel, gratitude to God, and explains why God alone merits gratitude through signs within people and around them.
rows.anchor: In the succeeding verses, it is being explained as to why only God is worthy of being grateful to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is urged to be patient, entrust the disbelievers’ fate to God, and disregard their demands for signs because abundant signs are already present.
rows.anchor: he should now consign their matter to God; He will decide about their fate; he should not pay heed to them if they are demanding signs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if all trees became pens and the seas, multiplied by seven, became ink, they still could not record all of God’s signs.
rows.anchor: even then all of God’s signs cannot be written.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These people break promises: hardship makes them promise obedience, but relief returns them to rebellion and forgetfulness, so no sign benefits habitual covenant-breakers.
rows.anchor: These people have a habit of breaking promises and are traitors.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day of Judgement, neither father nor son can help the other; each person is accountable for himself.
rows.anchor: neither a father will be of any use to any person nor his son; each person will be accountable for his own self.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unknown time of the Day of Judgement should not make anyone treat its warning as a baseless bluff, since other real events also have unknown timing.
rows.anchor: this should not deceive anyone that its threat is a mere bluff which has no basis.

none: Qur’anic text and its translation only
Qur’anic text and its translation only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The introduction ends at verse 11; Luqmān’s intervening counsel reinforces gratitude to God alone, and verse 20 resumes the argument from signs around people.
rows.anchor: The introductory part of this sūrah ended on verse 11 on the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 20 resumes the subject through signs around people in a tone of amazement and rebuke.
rows.anchor: The style adopted is that of amazement and rebuke.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are asked why they associate partners with God and worship them when God alone placed everything between heaven and earth in their service.
rows.anchor: all objects between the heavens and the earth that are serving them are put into this service for them by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asbagha literally means something wide and expansive and came to signify completion and perfection.
rows.anchor: something which is wide and expansive.” From here, it came to be used in the meaning of completion and perfection.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s completed favours encompass every aspect and include both apparent material blessings and intellectual and spiritual blessings.
rows.anchor: These favours are apparent and material as well as intellectual and spiritual.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human appearance, physique, limbs, food, clothing, hearing, sight, intellect, insight, and guidance are all favours from God, not another source.
rows.anchor: One’s appearance, physique, limbs, food, clothes and other similar things have been given by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God alone provides every favour, He alone deserves gratitude and no one can share that right.
rows.anchor: then it should only be He Who should be worthy of being grateful to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God’s existence and sole right to gratitude are established facts, some people dispute monotheism without argument, guidance, or illuminating scripture.
rows.anchor: they have neither any argument in their favour nor any guidance nor the support of any illuminating scripture.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about disputing concerning God, the governing noun is suppressed.
rows.anchor: The governing noun in ِ ّٰاللّٰہ ی ِ ف ُلِادَیُّج is suppressed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabian idolaters accepted God’s existence but disputed His oneness.
rows.anchor: The Idolaters of Arabia did not disbelieve in God. They only disputed His oneness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Without knowledge” means lacking reasoning, whether logical or scriptural; the same expression also occurs in verse 6.
rows.anchor: refer to a lack of reasoning whether its nature is logical or scriptural.
